newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk PM "probably" resigns Wednesday - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Turk PM "probably" resigns Wednesday - spokesman.

text.p: A spokesman for Turkey's ruling Islamists said Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan would probably visit President Suleyman Demirel on Wednesday to resign in a power-sharing deal with his pro-Western coalition partners.
"Yes, he will probably go there at 1800 (1500 GMT)," Welfare Party spokesman Salih Kapusuz said when asked by Reuters if Erbakan would take his resignation to the presidential palace.
Turkish newspapers said on Wednesday that Erbakan's True Path Party allies would pull out of the battered alliance if the prime minister did not quit by the end of the day.

"We have given Welfare until 2400 (2100 GMT). This is our last date and we will give no concessions on it. If Erbakan doesn't resign we will do what is needed," the Hurriyet daily quoted True Path senior MP Mehmet Golhan as saying.

Erbakan had previously agreed to step down and hand over power to True Path leader Tansu Ciller, who would head a caretaker government to take the country to early polls. But Erbakan has so far ducked the issue of quitting. He did not mention resigning in an hour-long speech to his MPs on Tuesday.
The government has been under intense pressure from the anti-Islamist army since February.
